Let’s talk about Chapter 7: Communication—Reducing Mental Friction.
You know, clear communication is kind of like oiling the gears in a well-run machine. When messages get tangled or expectations aren’t clear, your brain has to work extra hard just to keep up. That “mental friction” can really drain your energy—and before you know it, misunderstandings start to pile up.
Here’s something interesting: our brains process information best when it’s simple, concrete, and directly relevant. Think about the last time you got a long, jargon-filled email or an unclear request. Your mind had to sift through all that noise just to find what mattered. After a while, that’s exhausting—and it’s easy to make mistakes.
So, how can you cut down on that mental friction when you’re communicating? Try starting with concise, direct language. Get to the point and focus on what really matters. If you’ve got something complex to explain, break it down into smaller, bite-sized pieces. Use bullet points or keep your paragraphs short and clear. And don’t forget about those quick feedback loops—summarize the key points or ask a simple question to make sure everyone’s on track.
Visual tools can be a real game changer, too. Diagrams, checklists, even a simple flowchart can help everyone organize their thoughts. For example, putting a project timeline up on a shared screen gives the whole team an anchor—so you don’t have to keep repeating yourself or wonder if you’re all on the same page.
Another great habit is “closing the loop.” When you finish a task or make a decision, take a moment to send a quick confirmation. That way, no one’s left guessing, and you free up your mind for what’s next.
But communication isn’t just about facts and figures—it’s also about the emotional tone. A kind word, a genuine thank-you, or a little humor can completely change the way a message lands. Our brains don’t just remember what was said—they remember how it felt.
So, here’s the key takeaway: clear and caring communication lightens the mental load for everyone. It creates a shared mental map, making it so much easier to move forward together.
